authors_year: Brenguier, Campillo, Hadziioannou, Shapiro, Nadeau, Larose 2008
target_process: coseismic velocity reduction and postseismic relaxation (log(t) recovery) tracking afterslip on the San Andreas fault
region_site: Parkfield, San Andreas fault, California, USA
stack_scheme: 1550-day reference vs overlapping 5-day moving windows; 30-day time resolution
depth_sensitivity: Surface-wave sensitivity, shallow crust
dvv_amplitude: ~ -0.1% coseismic drop after 2004 M6 Parkfield (also 2003 San Simeon), relaxing as log(t)
uncertainty_treatment: Averaged over 78 receiver pairs plus 5-day segments
best_practice_note: Multi-year continuous monitoring averaged over many pairs (78) enables ~0.1% detection and correlation with GPS afterslip/tremor

target_process: coseismic velocity drop in a crustal-earthquake source region (fault-zone monitoring)
region_site: Mid-Niigata (Chuetsu) earthquake source region, Japan; F-Net station KZK (~24 km)
stack_scheme: Daily autocorrelations vs ~two-week pre-event reference; grid search (10000 trials, dv/v ±0.03)
depth_sensitivity: n/r (lapse-time dependence noted as future route to depth)
dvv_amplitude: -0.6% drop coinciding with the Mw 6.6 Mid-Niigata earthquake
uncertainty_treatment: ±0.1% fluctuation = inversion accuracy
best_practice_note: Single-station autocorrelation (passive image interferometry) avoids needing pairs; pick lapse window to exclude early scattered coda and stay above noise

target_process: sudden coseismic mean shear-wave velocity drop in earthquake source region
region_site: 2004 Mw 6.6 Mid-Niigata earthquake source region, Japan; 6 Hi-net/F-Net stations <25 km
stack_scheme: Daily auto-/cross-correlations inverted daily for 2 months pre/post; pre-event reference
depth_sensitivity: n/r
dvv_amplitude: Sudden drop of mean shear-wave velocity of a few tenths of a percent
uncertainty_treatment: Daily inversion fluctuations; consistency across 6 stations
best_practice_note: Coseismic drop confirmed with both AC and CC techniques across 6 stations, demonstrating robustness of passive interferometry

target_process: coseismic velocity decrease and postseismic recovery from repeating earthquakes
region_site: 1989 Mw 6.9 Loma Prieta aftershock zone, California (also Parkfield repeaters)
stack_scheme: Repeating-earthquake doublets; delays vs pre-mainshock repeaters
depth_sensitivity: Shallow concentration inferred (coda delays exceed direct-wave delays)
dvv_amplitude: Direct-S delays up to ~6 ms, S-coda delays >15 ms after Loma Prieta; coseismic decrease then recovery
uncertainty_treatment: High-precision relative delay via waveform cross-correlation of near-identical repeaters
best_practice_note: Repeating earthquakes give a co-located repeatable source; larger coda than direct-wave delays diagnose shallow change location

target_process: depth constraints on coseismic nonlinear strong-motion-induced velocity reduction
region_site: 2004 M6 Parkfield earthquake, San Andreas fault, California
stack_scheme: Repeating-earthquake travel-time delays before vs after mainshock
depth_sensitivity: Velocity change concentrates in top ~100 m (shallowmost crust)
dvv_amplitude: n/r (shallow S-wave traveltime delays; major shallow reduction)
uncertainty_treatment: Precise relative delay from near-identical repeating-earthquake waveforms
best_practice_note: Shows coseismic velocity reductions are dominantly a shallow (top ~100 m) nonlinear site effect — key for separating fault-zone vs near-surface signal

target_process: seasonal (hydrological) velocity variation; foundational passive-image-interferometry demonstration
region_site: Merapi Volcano, Indonesia
stack_scheme: Daily autocorrelations vs reference; single-day resolution
depth_sensitivity: Depth-dependent hydrological (groundwater-level) model
dvv_amplitude: Seasonal variations ~0.1% (measured at ~0.1% accuracy, 1-day resolution)
uncertainty_treatment: Accuracy ~0.1% velocity at single-day resolution
best_practice_note: Origin paper for passive image interferometry; seasonal/hydrological signals (~0.1%) must be modeled/removed to isolate tectonic change

authors_year: Rivet, Campillo, Shapiro, Cruz-Atienza, Radiguet, Cotte, Kostoglodov 2011
target_process: slow slip; nonlinear crustal deformation (strain-rate-dependent velocity change)
region_site: Guerrero, Mexico subduction zone (2006 M7.5 slow slip event)
depth_sensitivity: Surface waves sensitive to upper/middle crust ~5–20 km
dvv_amplitude: ~0.1% velocity decrease, far larger than volumetric strain (~1e-6)
uncertainty_treatment: n/r
best_practice_note: An aseismic SSE radiates no waves, so the velocity change cannot be a shaking/site response; time dependence tracks strain rate, evidencing crustal nonlinear elasticity

target_process: coseismic velocity drop and postseismic logarithmic healing
region_site: 2008 Iwate-Miyagi Nairiku earthquake (Mw 6.9), NE Japan
stack_scheme: Daily cross-correlations vs long-term reference Green's function
depth_sensitivity: Upper several hundred m at two stations; ~km depth indicated at a third
dvv_amplitude: Coseismic drops stronger at higher frequencies, concentrated in southern fault zone
uncertainty_treatment: Curves fit by model (coseismic drop + log postseismic recovery + seasonal)
best_practice_note: 190 station pairs in three frequency bands isolate drop + log recovery while modeling seasonal variation; frequency-dependence constrains depth

authors_year: Wang, Yao, van der Hilst et al. 2017
target_process: seasonal crustal velocity change (nationwide, includes Tohoku region)
region_site: Japan nationwide (718 Hi-net stations); notably Kyushu and Hokkaido
depth_sensitivity: Upper crust
dvv_amplitude: Seasonal dv/v ~0.01% (~1e-4) for Kyushu and NE Hokkaido
uncertainty_treatment: n/r
best_practice_note: Continental-scale single-station monitoring linking seasonal dv/v to environmental loads (rainfall/pore pressure, snow, sea level)

target_process: coseismic damage (near-surface weakening) and logarithmic healing
region_site: NE Japan (Honshu), KiK-net; 2011 Tohoku-Oki earthquake
depth_sensitivity: Upper ~100 m (borehole-to-surface S wave)
dvv_amplitude: ~10% reduction of shear-wave velocity in upper 100 m, then log healing
uncertainty_treatment: n/r
best_practice_note: Deconvolution interferometry between borehole and surface sensors isolates the upgoing S wave; maps a ~1200 km wide weakening zone with log-in-time healing

target_process: coseismic damage and multi-year postseismic healing (shallow S-wave velocity drop)
region_site: Western-Tottori region, Japan; KiK-net borehole (surface + 100 m); 2000 Mw 6.6 mainshock
stack_scheme: Coda deconvolution of surface vs 100-m borehole records
depth_sensitivity: Shallow ground 0–11 m (between surface and 100 m sensor)
dvv_amplitude: ~30% decrease in S-wave velocity after mainshock, recovering over several years
uncertainty_treatment: n/r
best_practice_note: Randomly scattered S-coda deconvolution of surface-borehole pair robustly isolates the very shallow (<11 m) layer of largest coseismic drop

target_process: coseismic velocity reduction and postseismic healing (mainshock + large aftershocks)
region_site: Southern Tohoku (Fukushima/Ibaraki), Japan; 58 Hi-net stations; 2011 Tohoku-Oki
depth_sensitivity: n/r
dvv_amplitude: Up to ~1.5–2% nearest mainshock, with gradual healing; drops after 11 Mar and 11 Apr events
uncertainty_treatment: n/r
best_practice_note: Single-station vertical autocorrelation avoids needing pairs; spatial dv/v correlates with static strain (GPS) and peak ground velocity

authors_year: Brenguier, Campillo, Takeda, Aoki, Shapiro, Briand, Emoto, Miyake 2014
target_process: dynamic stress; coseismic velocity drop / stress sensitivity of pressurized volcanic fluids
region_site: Volcanic/geothermal regions of Honshu, Japan; 2011 Mw 9.0 Tohoku-Oki
stack_scheme: Daily cross-correlations; linear inversion/regularization for continuous time series
depth_sensitivity: Relatively deep crustal volume (low-frequency 0.1–0.9 Hz Rayleigh waves)
dvv_amplitude: ~0.1% velocity decrease at volcanic regions after Tohoku-Oki
uncertainty_treatment: Stress sensitivity ~0.001 MPa^-1 inferred; detailed dv/v uncertainty n/r
best_practice_note: Low-frequency dense-network correlations map dynamic-stress-induced drops; concentration at volcanoes (not max shaking) reveals fluid-related stress sensitivity

authors_year: Gassenmeier, Sens-Schönfelder, Eulenfeld, Bartsch, Victor, Tilmann, Korn 2016
target_process: shaking-induced damage + postseismic healing (mesoscopic nonlinearity); thermal/environmental change
region_site: Station PATCX, Atacama Desert, Northern Chile (IPOC)
depth_sensitivity: Shallow: 90% of integrated sensitivity above ~114 m (6 Hz), ~168 m (4 Hz)
dvv_amplitude: Seasonal ~0.18%; transient coseismic drops ~0.49–0.62% for major earthquakes
uncertainty_treatment: Error from correlation-coefficient threshold ±1 s.d.; healing-fit errors (amplitude ~21%, decay time ~34%)
best_practice_note: 8 yr of single-station autocorrelations isolate damage/healing via mesoscopic nonlinearity after removing thermal seasonal signal; log-time recovery

target_process: depth-sensitivity methodology (coda-wave sensitivity vs depth)
region_site: Numerical 2-D elastic media (lunar-data illustration)
components: P and S (Vp/Vs=√3); Rayleigh fundamental mode dominates shallow
stack_scheme: Averaged over 10 random medium realizations per configuration
depth_sensitivity: Surface waves dominate first ~6 transport mean free times; lapse time localizes dv/v in depth
dvv_amplitude: n/r (methodological)
uncertainty_treatment: S.d. over 10 realizations; mean-free-path uncertainty ~2–15%
best_practice_note: Normalize by transport mean free time; use lapse-time dependence of coda dv/v to discriminate shallow (surface-wave) vs deep (body-wave) change

target_process: dv/v sensitivity-kernel theory (travel-time change of multiply scattered waves)
region_site: Theory / acoustic diffusion model
depth_sensitivity: Spatial sensitivity kernel (incl. depth) from probability a wave traversed a location in a lapse-time window
dvv_amplitude: n/r
uncertainty_treatment: n/r (analytical kernel)
best_practice_note: Foundational kernel for spatially localizing velocity changes from coda travel-time shifts under diffusion approximation; basis for later 3-D kernels

target_process: dv/v methodology (precision/stability of monitoring weak changes with noise correlation)
region_site: Laboratory scattering gel (ultrasonic)
depth_sensitivity: n/r (controlled lab medium)
dvv_amplitude: n/r (temperature-induced change)
uncertainty_treatment: Demonstrates stability when background noise-source structure is stable
best_practice_note: Full Green-function reconstruction is NOT required for monitoring; only relative stability of the noise-source structure — validates passive dv/v against active measurements

target_process: coseismic velocity change and its spatial distribution
region_site: Sichuan, China — 2008 Mw 7.9 Wenchuan earthquake fault zone
stack_scheme: Noise cross-correlation stacking; sub-array comparison (156 broadband stations)
depth_sensitivity: Mapped via sub-arrays; dv/v consistent with volumetric strain, not sediment response
dvv_amplitude: Velocity drop up to ~0.08% in fault region post-earthquake; pre-event fluctuations within ~0.02%
uncertainty_treatment: Pre-earthquake fluctuation (~0.02%) used as baseline/noise reference
best_practice_note: Compare across spatial sub-arrays to retrieve spatial pattern; relate to modeled volumetric strain to attribute change to in-situ strain not sediments

target_process: coseismic velocity reduction + postseismic recovery / long-lived change
region_site: Epicentral region of 2008 Mw 7.9 Wenchuan earthquake, China
depth_sensitivity: Most prominent in 2–4 s band (~1–4 km), indicating depth-localized upper-crustal change
dvv_amplitude: Coseismic reduction up to ~0.2%; initial recovery then long-lived reduction
uncertainty_treatment: Pre-event period as baseline (no obvious precursor)
best_practice_note: Use multiple period bands of three-component correlations to separate depth-dependent dv/v; long-lived reduction interpreted as incomplete healing

authors_year: Mao, Mordret, Campillo, Fang, van der Hilst 2020
target_process: dv/v methodology (wavelet cross-spectrum travel-time change; frequency-dependent dv/v)
region_site: Salton Sea Geothermal Field, California (2009–2011)
depth_sensitivity: Frequency-resolved dt(f,t) discriminates dv/v at different frequencies/depths; less spectral smearing than MWCS
dvv_amplitude: n/r (method demonstration)
uncertainty_treatment: Wavelet-coherence thresholding and amplitude-based weighting
best_practice_note: Wavelet cross-spectrum gives optimal time-frequency resolution, handles dispersion + cycle skipping (2-D unwrapping), recovers dt more stably than stretching/MWCS

target_process: postseismic healing / velocity recovery (transient damage + groundwater drainage)
region_site: Bhote Koshi catchment, Nepal Himalaya — 2015 Mw 7.8 Gorkha earthquake
depth_sensitivity: Near-surface; coupled shallow-damage + hydrological model
dvv_amplitude: n/r (modeled co/postseismic drop and recovery)
uncertainty_treatment: Model-based separation of damage (NLME) vs hydrological dv/v
best_practice_note: Correct for non-linear mesoscopic elasticity (NLME) damage recovery before interpreting residual dv/v; relaxation timescales ~1 yr (mainshock), 1–3 days (aftershocks), 4–6 months (monsoon)

target_process: coseismic velocity drop and recovery
region_site: South Napa, California (2014 Mw 6.0 South Napa earthquake)
depth_sensitivity: Likely within seismogenic depth (≤10 km); poorly constrained
dvv_amplitude: ~0.08% velocity reduction after the earthquake
uncertainty_treatment: n/r
best_practice_note: NCFs computed with MSNoise; band-pass 0.08–2.0 Hz then decimate to 20 Hz

authors_year: Hillers, Campillo, Brenguier, Moreau, Agnew, Ben-Zion 2019
target_process: fault-zone monitoring; velocity changes interpreted as response to deep aseismic creep
region_site: San Jacinto fault zone, California (after 2010 M7.2 El Mayor-Cucapah, M5.4 Collins Valley)
stack_scheme: Average-waveform reference for stretching; MWCS also applied
depth_sensitivity: Top ~10 km (above proposed deep creep source below 10 km)
dvv_amplitude: n/r (two tens-of-days episodes of reduced velocity)
uncertainty_treatment: Cross-check between time-domain stretching and frequency-domain MWCS
best_practice_note: Resolves two successive ~tens-of-days velocity-reduction episodes over a 200-day window around April 2010

target_process: coseismic velocity drop plus seasonal variation; crustal rheology
region_site: L'Aquila region, central Italy (2009 Mw 6.3 L'Aquila earthquake)
depth_sensitivity: n/r
dvv_amplitude: ~0.3% coseismic drop; ~0.05% seasonal cyclic variation
uncertainty_treatment: n/r
best_practice_note: 17-year single-station record separating coseismic from temperature-driven seasonal signals

authors_year: Wang, Campillo, Brenguier, Lecointre, Takeda, Hashima 2019
target_process: coseismic damage (short period) and postseismic/static-strain change (long period) across the crust
region_site: NE Honshu, Japan (2011 Mw 9.0 Tohoku-Oki earthquake)
depth_sensitivity: Entire crust; long-period (to 50 s) samples below ~5 km; coseismic amplitude decreases with depth
dvv_amplitude: n/r (short-period drops in strong-shaking region; long-period drops delayed up to ~6 months)
uncertainty_treatment: n/r
best_practice_note: Combine short-period sensors with tiltmeters as long-period seismometers to extend depth sensitivity through the full crust

target_process: coseismic velocity drop and rapid postseismic recovery in fault-zone material
region_site: Ridgecrest, California (2019 Mw 7.1 Ridgecrest earthquake)
stack_scheme: 10-min stacks; adaptive Gaussian smoothing (20 min growing to 24 hr over 3 days)
depth_sensitivity: Shallow upper crust ~1–3 km
dvv_amplitude: ~2% regional average; up to ~8% near rupture-arrest and Coso geothermal region
uncertainty_treatment: Standard deviations tracked; stabilized via smoothing
best_practice_note: Exploit abundant aftershock waveforms (autocorrelations and P/S conversions) instead of ambient noise for high-time-resolution monitoring

target_process: coseismic velocity drop and postseismic recovery (months)
region_site: Ridgecrest fault zone, California (2019 Mw 7.1 Ridgecrest earthquake)
stack_scheme: Daily autocorrelation functions vs mean waveform
depth_sensitivity: Shallow crust surrounding the fault zone
dvv_amplitude: n/r (short-term drop near rupture; none beyond ~50 km; max change scales with log distance and peak dynamic strain)
uncertainty_treatment: n/r
best_practice_note: Velocity drop confined within ~50 km of rupture; recovery 1–3 months depending on slip and triggered-slip context

authors_year: Sheng, Mordret, Sager, Brenguier, Boué, Rousset, Vernon, Higueret, Ben-Zion 2022
target_process: slow slip event detection; fault-zone monitoring
region_site: San Jacinto fault, Anza seismic gap, Southern California
depth_sensitivity: A few km depth; reduced near-surface sensitivity
dvv_amplitude: dV/V inferred from volumetric strain of a ~Mw 5.1 / ~0.2 m SSE (early 2014, ~2 months)
uncertainty_treatment: Inverse travel-time uncertainties used as weights in misfit
best_practice_note: Use repeatable train-generated tremors as a stable high-frequency source; dV/V derived via volumetric-strain simulations

target_process: postseismic healing (Hector Mine, El Mayor-Cucapah relaxation) plus hydrological/seasonal change
region_site: California (statewide, ~700 stations)
depth_sensitivity: Upper ~500 m (near-surface)
dvv_amplitude: Up to ~2% (seasonal/drought); decade-scale postseismic relaxation near Hector Mine and El Mayor-Cucapah
uncertainty_treatment: Model comparison (thermoelastic, hydrological diffusion, slow-dynamics healing); formal dv/v errors n/r
best_practice_note: Separate climate (rain/drought) from coseismic/postseismic signals; multi-decade statewide single-station monitoring with SeisNoise.jl
